message:
The `excludedModules` parameter in `SystemDocumentationMojo` was only accepting values from the Maven plugin configuration block and did not support Maven properties passed via command line using `-D` flags.

## Problem

Previously, users could only exclude modules by configuring the plugin in their `pom.xml`:

```xml
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.skyve</groupId>
    <artifactId>skyve-maven-plugin</artifactId>
    <configuration>
        <excludedModules>module1,module2</excludedModules>
    </configuration>
</plugin>
```

Command-line usage was ignored:
```bash
mvn skyve:systemDocumentation -DexcludedModules=module1,module2  # This was ignored
```

## Solution

Added the `property` attribute to the `@Parameter` annotation:

```java
// Before
@Parameter
private String excludedModules;

// After  
@Parameter(property = "excludedModules")
private String excludedModules;
```

## Benefits

- **Command-line support**: Users can now dynamically exclude modules from the command line
- **CI/CD friendly**: Build scripts can easily pass different excluded modules for different environments
- **Backward compatible**: Existing configuration-based usage continues to work unchanged
- **Standard Maven pattern**: Follows the same pattern used by other Maven plugins and parameters in this codebase

## Usage

Both approaches now work:

```bash
# Command line (now supported)
mvn skyve:systemDocumentation -DexcludedModules=module1,module2

# Configuration (still supported)  
<configuration><excludedModules>module1,module2</excludedModules></configuration>
```

This change enables flexible module exclusion while maintaining full backward compatibility with existing configurations.
